title: foundry plan.json, version 1
description: <foundry dir>/plan.json: the seam between the architect, the foreman and the hooks. The architect drafts it in plan mode; the foreman owns it after that; the hooks treat it as read-only. See adr/0001-design-phase.md, section 8.

version.description: Plan file format version. It goes up whenever a field is added.

goal.description: The run's goal, as the owner gave it.

architecture.description: Repo-relative path of the architecture doc, as recorded in <repo>/.claude/foundry.json.

approval.description: Set once, at plan time, by the foreman: "owner" exactly when the plan has a wave-0 crew, otherwise "auto". Mid-run design slices never change it. The schema checks only that "owner" implies a wave-0 crew, because the file can't show which crews a mid-run slice added.

approvedAt.description: Set by the foreman, as an RFC 3339 date-time with a time-zone offset (JSON Schema format date-time), for example 2026-10-26T14:03:00+01:00 or 2026-10-26T13:03:00Z. A date-time with no offset is invalid. An "auto" run gets the time the foreman logged the plan; an "owner" run gets the time the owner approved. Null only while a run waits for the owner; while approval is "owner" and this is null, the run-level approval gate refuses every lead in the plan.

agentCap.description: The most agents the plan may estimate in total; a plan over it is re-planned. The total is the sum of the crews' estAgents and isn't stored. Default 40, from agentCap in <repo>/.claude/foundry.json.

maxParallelCrews.description: The most crews that may be running at once; extra crews in a wave queue. Default 4, from maxParallelCrews in <repo>/.claude/foundry.json.

crews.description: One entry per crew. Within a wave, the order of this array is the queue order: crews beyond maxParallelCrews start in this order as running ones merge. The agent total is the sum of estAgents; it isn't stored.

allOf.$comment: approval "owner" implies a wave-0 crew (ADR-0001 section 8). The reverse holds at plan time only, so it isn't checked.
approvedAt is null only while a run waits for the owner, and an auto run never waits (ADR-0001 section 6).

slug.description: The crew's name, and the name of its foundry:lead: lowercase letters and digits in words joined by single hyphens, never ending in -<digits>. The -<digits> ending is reserved because a successor lead is named <slug>-<n> and the hooks gate a successor as its base slug. safeName in hooks/register.ts leaves such a name of up to 100 characters unchanged, so report folders match the slug.

wave.description: The wave the crew runs in. Wave 0 holds the change work and merges before any other wave starts; each wave merges before the next starts. A mid-run design slice goes to the earliest wave that hasn't started yet, and the crews that depend on it move one wave later.

verdict.description: What kind of crew this is. "design": writes ADRs and contract tests (a wave-0 crew, or a mid-run design slice). "change": a build crew whose module's design changed, so it runs after the design crew. "extend": a build crew working inside the existing design.

modules.description: Module names from the architecture doc's module map.

owns.description: Path globs the crew owns. No two crews may own the same file.

doneCheck.description: The command that proves the crew is done, runnable with the crew's own access.

doneCheckProved.description: Whether the architect ran doneCheck once while planning.

estAgents.description: Estimated agent count for the crew. The plan's agent total is the sum of these and isn't stored.

ownerApproval.description: Optional; mid-run design slices only. The foreman sets "pending" when the slice must wait for the owner (one of the owner triggers in ADR-0001 section 4 applies), and "approved" when the owner answers. While it is "pending", the crew-level approval gate refuses this crew's lead. Absent on every other crew.

status.description: Set by the foreman as crews start and merge. The hooks only read it.

allOf.$comment: Wave 0 holds the change work: ADRs, the architecture-doc change and the contract tests (ADR-0001 section 5), which is what a design crew does (section 8). A change crew runs after the design crew, so it can't be in wave 0. A design crew may sit in a later wave: a mid-run slice goes to the earliest wave that hasn't started (section 7).
ownerApproval is for mid-run design slices only (ADR-0001 sections 7 and 8).
